title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen (GQA/MQA tuning, kernels, KV cache, batching)
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: Several production customers and internal perf canaries showed suboptimal throughput and occasional latency spikes when serving specific open models (Llama 2 variants, Mistral 7B/7B-v0, and Qwen-7B) under mixed QKV/sequence length workloads. Root causes included suboptimal kernel selection for GQA/MQA weight formats, KV cache growth and alignment issues for multi-query attention (MQA), and poor batching shapes caused by model-specific tokenization/temperature hotspots.

Motivation: Reduce per-token CPU/GPU cycles and tail latency for model variants we routinely serve, while preserving exactness for deterministic small models and maximizing throughput for high-concurrency customers. This PR implements a set of targeted runtime changes and model heuristics to improve kernel selection, scheduling, KV cache layout, and continuous batching heuristics.

What I changed (summary):
- Added model profiling metadata that marks model families with preferred attention formats (GQA vs MQA) and preferred kernel backends. This metadata is collected at model-load time and used by the kernel selector.
- Kernel selector: introduce a lightweight cost model that picks quantized GEMM and attention kernels based on sequence length distribution and QKV packing. New rule: prefer MQA-optimized attention kernels for Qwen-7B variants and GQA-optimized kernels for specific Llama checkpoints.
- KV cache layout: for MQA models we realign KV buffers to 256B boundaries and switch to an interleaved layout that reduces memory copies when slicing during generation. Also added a cache-growth cap heuristic that triggers prefix compaction at 50k tokens per session to avoid memory fragmentation for long-running chat sessions.
- Continuous batching: updated the batching scheduler to use per-model micro-buckets for short sequences and an adaptive cutoff that avoids merging short high-priority requests with long background batches. This reduces head-of-line blocking and improves p95 latency under mixed workloads.
- Scheduling: enhanced the request prioritizer to consider model-specific latency targets and kernel warmup state; warmup-preferring scheduler will create small warmup batches when switching kernels for a model variant.
- Tests & benchmarks: added unit tests for KV layout transforms, integration tests with synthetic seqlen distributions, and a perf harness comparing baseline vs optimized kernels. Included benchmark artifacts and a perf/README with guidance.

Behavioral notes and compatibility:
- No API surface changes. All heuristics are runtime-only and opt-in via model metadata flags; default behaviour remains unchanged unless the model manifest includes the new tuning flags. For managed models in the catalog, we've enabled the flags for verified Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants.
- There is a small (~0.5%) numerical difference for a micro-quantized GEMM path when using the MQA interleaved KV layout for certain 8-bit quantized weights. We validated that generation quality (perplexity and end-to-end eval prompts) is within noise for all affected models; see perf section below.

Results (canary):
- Llama-2-70B-ish family (GQA preferred): 12-18% throughput improvement on A100 p4d for typical seqlen=128 workloads; p95 latency unchanged.
- Mistral-7B / Mistral-7B-v0 (MQA tuning): 22% throughput gain and 10% p95 latency reduction on T4-like hardware for chat-style mixed seqlen workload.
- Qwen-7B: 15% throughput improvement, 8% p95 reduction.
- End-to-end eval (1000 prompt set): generation BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-score changes are within ±0.3 absolute; no regressions flagged by quality monitor.

Checklist: 
- [x] Runtime metadata and kernel selector implementation
- [x] KV cache layout changes + compaction heuristic
- [x] Batching scheduler updates
- [x] Unit/integration tests
- [x] Canary benchmark and perf writeup
- [x] Docs: updated runtime tuning README and model onboarding notes

Related: ENG-1842 (model-onboarding perf), ENG-1901 (scheduler improvements), SUP-1123 (customer-reported Qwen latencies).

Notes for reviewers: Look for the kernel selector fallthrough logic (we added explicit unit tests). Pay attention to the KV layout code path under runtime/kv_cache/mqa_aligned.cpp (small but performance-critical). The perf harness lives under perf-canary/model-tuning/ and contains the scripts used for the numbers above.

Merge plan: Squash merge. Canary to Dedicated staging pool for 48h, roll to hosted catalog models with feature flag off-by-default, enable for verified models after successful canary.
